newsitem.title: UK: Ldn Freight-Early Panamaxes short in the Atlantic.
newsitem.headline: Ldn Freight-Early Panamaxes short in the Atlantic.

text.p: A shortage of early modern Panamaxes in the Atlantic was again evident and caused the BFI to rise 4 points to 1286.

But in most other respects the freight market was dull with few immediate signs of improvement for owners of Capers and Handy-sizes. There were some indications that Panamax rates in the Far East might be softening.

Brokers noted a number of June/early July enquiries for Panamaxes for grain from US Gulf, and more especially E Coast S America, still unfixed. It was believed likely that rates would continue to edge forwards for loading positions upto mid-July, although few fixtures have yet been reported. Brokers suspect that a number of deals have been concluded privately.

In the north Atlantic charterers were again active covering tonnage US Gulf/Egypt. It was said that Continental booked Mariann 64,064 dwt at a firmer rate, but full details were elusive. Continental confirmed their fixture of Petriana 64,911 dwt delivery US Gulf June/July trip Japan at $11,250 daily plus $200,000 bonus, a solid rate for a relatively deep, heavy-consumption, over-age vessel. Another 1981-built Panamax, Sun P 65,738 dwt, was fixed delivery prompt Lisbon for 2 or 3 laden legs redelivery Atlantic at $8,750 daily by Mosvold/Mega Pacific.

Intended trading was said to be St Lawrence/Saudi Arabia grain, followed by Richards Bay/Continent coal. In a softer Panamax mart in the East Halla were said to have taken Imperial 68,676 dwt in direct continuation for a NoPac round at $9,000 daily. Fresh enquiry included Korea Line 54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan for 15/25 July, IrisL 60,000 corn Up River and Necochea or Bahia Blanca to Japan any August, Dreyfus 7,000,000/1m cft Mississippi/Ireland option WCUK 1/7 July, and Pacnav 27/30,000 dwt delivery St Lawrence 1/15 July trip E C Mexico.

Here were several rumoured fixtures, but reliable information was lacking. In the Atlantic Veni 172,278 dwt was linked with Cetragpa for Tubarao/Rotterdam, and Europa 110,000 dwt with Bocimar Boca Grande/Dunkirk East. Pan Ocean were said to have fixed the Docenave relet Anangel solidarity 160,000 dwt Brazil/Far East at $19,000 daily plus unknown bonus. In the East Docenave were believed to have taken Karoo 161,000 dwt delivery W Australia mid July for a trip to Brazil at $13,000 daily followed by a trip to the Continent at $15,750 daily. Capeestrel 161,000 dwt, open Kaohsiung end June, was understood fixed on private terms. Among the Panamaxes it was rumoured that Eleranta 73,222 dwt was fixed prompt Japan at a significantly lower level for an Australian round, possibly about $9,000 daily. Bocimar booked a similar vessel, Galene 73,650 dwt, delivery prompt Japan for a trip via Indonesia to Hongkong with coal at $9,000 daily, down $750 daily from a round voyage rate agreed on subjects by this vessel a week ago. The weaker cnditions were said to reflect lack of demand by Japanese coal charterers.

Aimcor fixed Clymene 63,300 dwt delivery USWC end June trip Continent with Petcoke at $6,750 daily plus $140,000 bonus. Armada fixed Gema Pertiwi 64,000 dwt delivery S E Asia for ironore from Dampier to Eregli at $6,000 daily. Agia Dynamis 68,000 dwt was reported fixed for coal from Richards Bay to Dunkirk at $7.10, and Premuda booked a Docenave-relet 75,000 dwt Panamax with coal Mobile/Brazil on private terms. x
